answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

SCOPE & DATA
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above the catalogue magnitude of completeness Mc).
- Pumping (15.96 days): injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 (net extraction).
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue magnitudes are calibrated, so these are the trustworthy numbers):
  b      Sigma      P(Mw>=5.5)/yr   P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198       5.236e-06                         0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922        0.0002155                         0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474         0.0006484                         0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at/above catalogue Mc, so it OVER-COUNTS and is only an upper bound, not calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

INTERPRETATION: The calibrated (LBNL catalogue) annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 earthquake is very low — 1.2e-4/yr at b=1.0, rising to 1.47e-2/yr only in the low-b (0.65) scenario. The DAS-based figure (0.078/yr) is an uncalibrated upper bound that over-counts because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all detections are treated as catalogue-complete events.
